content:
Maya Chen: Hey team, multiple customers reporting 502/503s from the hosted inference API starting ~08:10 UTC. Example request id: req-0a1b2c. They see a gateway 502 with body 'control-plane dependency failure'. Can we triage?
Samir Patel: Seen a couple similar alerts. Are these all for the same region? Any correlation ids or model names?
Maya Chen: Mostly us-east-1. Correlation ids: req-0a1b2c, req-0a1b2d, req-0a1b2f. Model ids: rdx-llama-13b and rdx-3b, but looks upstream control-plane auth/session calls failing before model selection.
Priya Rangan: Copying logs from the gateway:
```
2026-03-14T08:10:12.123Z ERROR gateway request_id=req-0a1b2c status=502 upstream_error="controlplane: auth/session: timeout after 5s"
2026-03-14T08:10:12.125Z WARN routing policy fetch failed: configdb timeout (500ms) attempts=3
2026-03-14T08:10:12.126Z INFO fallback route used? false
```
Samir Patel: That first line looks like session store (controlplane auth) timed out. Config DB timeouts right after. Could be DB overloaded or a cascading connection pool exhaustion on the control plane.
Jordi Park: @Priya can you paste the control-plane pod logs and the config DB metric snapshot (conn count, p95 latency) around 08:09-08:12?
Priya Rangan: Pasting excerpt from control-plane auth service: 
```
[2026-03-14T08:09:58Z] WARN session-store request_id=req-0a1b2c getSession timeout after 5s
[2026-03-14T08:10:00Z] ERROR session-store pool exhausted: max=120 active=121 waiting=34
[2026-03-14T08:10:05Z] ERROR downstream configdb query failed: timeout=500ms conn_wait=1200ms
```
Maya Chen: Customers are upset — some are hitting request retries which then create higher load. One customer reported degraded latency since 08:05 and then 5xx spikes at 08:10.
Samir Patel: Quick triage steps: 1) confirm config DB health (RDS/managed) 2) check control-plane service horizontal autoscaling 3) look at circuit breakers in gateway 4) enable routing fallback to static rules to bypass routing-policy calls.
eng-oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2026-234, severity=P2, paged oncall.
Jordi Park: I'm oncall. Priya — did the routing-policy service call config DB often per request? If routing policy does a per-request lookup it can amplify load.
Priya Rangan: Yes, current policy: per-request policy fetch from configdb unless cache hit. Cache TTL is low (15s) because of rapid rollouts. Cache miss rate spiked to 84% at 08:09.
Samir Patel: That explains it: per-request DB queries + small pool -> exhaustion -> session store timeouts -> gateway 502.
Maya Chen: Mitigation in progress: 1) increase control-plane DB connection pool on routing-policy and session-store from 120 -> 200 (hotfix) 2) bump cache TTL from 15s -> 2m to reduce QPS 3) enable static route fallback for hosted-api for 5min to avoid policy calls. Priya/Tony to apply.
Priya Rangan: Rolling update applied to routing-policy (scaled +2 replicas) and cache TTL bumped. Also toggled static fallback in gateway config: `routing_policy.call_enabled=false` for hosts in us-east-1 for 5m.
Maya Chen: After the change, error rate dropped to baseline within ~60s. Customers reporting recovered.
Samir Patel: Follow-ups: - Postmortem to explain root cause (cache TTL + per-request DB queries + small pool) - Add circuit breaker on routing-policy calls before session-store to fail fast - Consider read-replica and connection pooling improvements on config DB - Add alert when cache-miss rate > 60% for >2m
Jordi Park: I'll own the postmortem and remediation ticket. Created ENG-2026-817 (postmortem + action items).
Maya Chen: Recording quick repro steps for engineers: 1) run the following load test against routing-policy endpoint with low cache TTL to simulate cache miss storm: 
```
ab -n 10000 -c 200 http://controlplane-us-east1.internal/routing-policy?key=somekey
```
2) Observe pool exhaustion logs in auth/session service and resulting gateway 502s.
Priya Rangan: Also note suspicious behavior: some clients were aggressively retrying on 502 with no jitter which amplified the spike. Need guidance for customers about exponential backoff.
Maya Chen: Communication: I posted a status update to affected customers and marked incident as resolved after verification. Will follow-up with a changelog entry for the hotfix.
Jordi Park: Action items assigned: Priya -> implement adaptive cache TTL and circuit breaker (ETA 2d). Samir -> DB pooling + read replica review (ETA 3d). Maya -> customer comms and KB on best retry practices (ETA EOD).
Maya Chen: Thanks all :thumbsup: Will drop a summary in #postmortems when ENG-2026-817 is ready.

eng-oncall-bot: Reminder to attach logs and correlation ids to the incident ticket."
